A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–J support reliable comparison. V5 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V4 reports original Procgen experiments, clustering and ablation analyses, and a study with 15 human evaluators in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V5 retains those original experiments and human evaluations, and adds quantitative Stop-Grad comparisons and temporal-coherence results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The FDR network, vector quantization, policy-feature fusion, losses, and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged. Renaming the control factor from f_control to lambda_ctrl and expanding explanations do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CoinRun, FruitBot, Jumper, and Ninja, with human evaluations covering the same three games. Appendix F extends analysis within existing coverage. Newly stated evaluator qualifications describe the existing study rather than establish a changed population.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds Stop-Grad to Table 4's Trained-versus-Raw comparison and compares Ours against Stop-Grad in new Table 5. Although Stop-Grad already appeared in Appendix C.2, its participation in these quantitative comparisons is new. PPO and the five dimensionality-reduction baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Table 5 evaluates Episode Cluster Entropy and Temporal Cluster Agreement at lags 3 and 6, averaged over episodes. These extend the evaluation protocol; the retained sampling procedures, training settings, and 50,000-state cluster analysis are not substantively revised.

E4.justification: Appendix F extends the existing stop-gradient ablation with quantitative cluster-transition, pixel-distance, and temporal-coherence analyses across three games. Appendix A also adds brief hyperparameter-sensitivity observations. Earlier state-count, visualization-seed, and embedding-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The disclosed seeds, three-run evaluations, SEM reporting in Table 2 and Figure E.1, and standard deviations in Table 4 are retained. New Table 5 reports episode averages without introducing uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or additional run-count information.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds Stop-Grad results and changes Ninja's trained-model pixel-distance mean from 141.50 to 141.57. New Table 5 reports lower ECE and higher TCA@3/6 for Ours across all three games; for example, Ninja ECE is 1.3086 for Ours versus 1.5505 for Stop-Grad.

T1.justification: Appendix F introduces definitions of ECE as episode cluster-distribution entropy and TCA@k as the fraction of same-cluster frame pairs at lag k. These are limited mathematical-definition additions; Appendix B's similarity-preservation and online k-means theorems and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about intrinsic semantic clustering, stable FDR-based analysis, and policy interpretability remain unchanged. The introduction clarifies semantic clustering and the integrated architecture without materially changing the contribution scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds interpretations distinguishing policy-induced structure from the module's further contribution to temporal coherence, and explains Jumper's lower ECE through shorter episodes. Section 5 adds concrete future directions involving alternative affinities and automated explanations.

D1.justification: V5 adds an explicit method-repository link, approximately 15-minute annotation-effort information, evaluator eligibility details, and code/configuration/license disclosures in the checklist. Existing architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, and per-run training time remain unchanged. Some checklist documentation claims lack corresponding details.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds VQ-VAE application literature covering images, video, speech, and model-based RL. V5 also adds Patil et al.'s contrastive-abstraction reference and replaces the introductory Ernst–Louette citation with François-Lavet et al. The main positioning against earlier DRL visualization work is retained.

P1.justification: V5 contains localized rewrites and expanded explanations, notation and citation-format updates, acknowledgments, and a new checklist. The main Sections 1–6 and appendices A–J retain their overall organization; the scientific narrative is not extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: V5 expands and restructures Table 4, adds Table 5, and renumbers the later cluster-description tables. Figure 6 gains cluster labels, mean-image displays in Figures 3, G.2, and G.4 receive visual updates, and several captions and figure placements change.

improvement.justification: The added Stop-Grad comparisons and temporal-coherence measurements in Appendix F strengthen the earlier qualitative ablation, while the explicit code link and evaluator/annotation disclosures improve transparency. These are limited gains: Table 5 provides no uncertainty estimates, and the new checklist overstates some documentation, including reported total GPU-days.
